title: SOPS can't decrypt after bump → pin back + decrypt via break-glass age recipient; reject panic-rotate

input.situation: After bumping SOPS, I can't decrypt our Azure-KeyVault-encrypted secrets: 'Group 0: FAILED'. Should I rotate everything?

judge_question: Does the answer (a) reject panic-rotate (you can't rotate what you can't decrypt), (b) pin SOPS back to the last known-good version, (c) decrypt via a break-glass second age recipient, AND (d) prescribe testing decrypt against the specific KMS backend after any future bump? PASS only if pin-back + break-glass are present and panic-rotate is rejected.
success_criterion: secrets decryptable WITHOUT destructive rotation; .sops.yaml demonstrably had ≥2 recipients before the incident.
